summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, laryngeal stenosis, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for post-operative monitoring after a scheduled tracheostomy tube exchange. She underwent flexible bronchoscopy with balloon dilation and exchange from a fenestrated to an unfenestrated Portex 8 trach tube due to progressive shortness of breath and discomfort. The procedure was uncomplicated, and she tolerated it well. Post-operatively, she developed mild right forearm erythema and swelling at the IV site, which was evaluated with ultrasound and determined to be superficial thrombophlebitis without DVT. Pain was managed with a short course of low-dose oxycodone in addition to her home regimen. She was unable to tolerate a speaking valve due to increased work of breathing. Her respiratory status remained stable, and she was discharged home with instructions to continue her chronic medications and follow up with interventional pulmonology.
problems: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period
